question: An operations director presents the results of a two-week Claude pilot to the executive team, showing only the three best outputs the team produced. What is the greatest risk in communicating the results this way?
options: A) The pilot's outputs cannot be reused afterwards, because examples shown to executives must be regenerated.
B) Executives will conclude the pilot used the wrong tool and will ask for a different vendor to be evaluated instead.
C) The team will be required to repeat the whole pilot from the start before any rollout decision is taken.
D) Executives set expectations from unrepresentative examples and are surprised when routine output needs editing.
correct_answers: D) Executives set expectations from unrepresentative examples and are surprised when routine output needs editing.
explanations: There is no such constraint on reusing output that has been presented.
Strong examples do not prompt a vendor challenge; the problem is that they are not representative.
A repeat pilot is not the inherent risk; misplaced expectations are.
Correct. Cherry-picked results overstate the typical case, and the gap surfaces later as disappointment or lost trust.
